content: In youth with Type 1 Diabetes, nephropathy treatment should involve the consideration of an ACE inhibitor or an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) when the albumin-to-creatinine ratio exceeds 30 mg/g. This diagnosis must be confirmed by at least two out of three elevated urine samples collected over a six-month period. The use of these medications helps to normalize blood pressure and reduce albumin excretion, which are critical in managing diabetic nephropathy. However, due to the teratogenic risks associated with ACE inhibitors and ARBs, individuals of childbearing age should avoid these medications unless they are using reliable contraception to prevent pregnancy.
